instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Slice the tops off the tomatoes and keep each top with its tomato. Scoop out the pulp and seeds into a bowl, leaving thick walls so the tomatoes keep their shape. Finely chop the thicker pulp and put it back in the bowl. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and garlic with a pinch of salt and pepper about 6 minutes, until soft and just starting to brown. Add the tomato pulp and juice and cook 8 to 10 minutes, until slightly reduced. Let it cool 5 minutes.
In a large bowl, mix the beef, sausage meat, breadcrumbs, herbes de Provence, 1 tbsp chopped parsley, 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Stir in the cooled tomato mixture.

Season the inside of each tomato shell with salt and pepper. Fill the shells with the meat mixture, letting it mound a little over the rim, and put the tops back on. Set them in an 8 by 8 inch baking dish and drizzle with the remaining 1 tbsp oil. If you'd like, fill the tomatoes up to a day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge, then bake as below.
Bake about 1 hour, until lightly browned. The filling should reach about 160°F; a thermometer is optional. Without one, cut one tomato open to check that the filling is firm and no longer pink.
Sprinkle with the remaining 1 tbsp parsley and serve with the pan juices spooned over. Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge.
method_notes: Vanilla Bean Cuisine is the lead (4.96 from 50 ratings), with a no pre-cooked beef and sausage filling baked in an 8 by 8 dish. Pardon Your French (4.2 from 17) uses beef, rice, egg and parmesan and bakes 1 1/2 hours; it was used as a cross-check on the rice-and-herb style, but not followed. The lead says traditionally served over rice; this version serves with the pan juices. Total time is about 90 minutes because of the hour in the oven, mostly hands off.
